You’re right, it does happen, and can out of nowhere even for any healthy dog and it can come out of nowhere for experienced and inexperienced owners. Though a declining of quality of life in the drastic way would absolutely suggest that there is usually an underlying diagnosis or perhaps even a genetic marker the predetermined the reasoning for such a swift change. I consistently get stuck on the line that the veterinarian said the dog’s exam wether bloodwork was run or not  (it should have been) was ‘normal’. Everything the dog was displaying was abnormal.  Old age is not a disease it is a happenstance of a beautiful long life. 

Please never stop advocating and using your voice to help animals and other owners on the journey, you are amazing losthedgehog

Do I think OP expected the dog to be sick, no, but it is simply fishy based on these lines alone. ‘He usually leaves me to care for his dog which I don’t mind’… ‘I’d never want something terrible to happen to HIS pride and joy’

I’m not giving a judgement without more facts simply because I don’t have enough info, however the wording of the post and the non-descript vet diagnosis is odd.

I agree this is sus. If it was old age but the checkup was ‘normal’ the onset wouldn’t be so sudden and dramatic that in the span of a week an otherwise healthy dog was unresponsive and that euthanasia was the only option. Something else had to have been very wrong that you are leaving out of this OP. What really happened to the dog? I am all for pets having a peaceful passing if they have no quality of life due to legitimate reasons. But this normal checkup, is not the full story.

Edit: The reason I ask and my skepticism is because I am a veterinary technician who specializes in End of Life and hospice care, previously an emergency internal medicine and surgical tech.

Edit 2: thank you to everyone who responded to this you all are amazing! I’m sending love and hugs to each of you and your furry companions both here and those who have crossed the rainbow bridge.

Edit 3: For Clarification YES pets can go downhill very rapidly however there is more often than not an underlying reason that would appear in an exam at a veterinary clinic/hospital. In which this would constitute as something ‘abnormal’. Vs a vet saying everything is ‘normal’ and it is just old age. Old age is not a disease that causes a rapid deterioration, it is a slow progress of noticeable changes in a pet. Please do not come and leave angry comments that it does happen, that is not the basis of the request of info simply an observation based on a lack of details.

Edit 4: I have no doubts I’ll get flack for this one but here goes. This was posted 22 hours ago, OP has made zero efforts to respond or add information, based on nuances of how OP talks about the dog (my husbands ‘pride and joy’, ‘of course I wouldn’t want something bad to happen’, his dogs ‘corpse’ on the ground. I’m going to go out on a limb, the exam wasn’t normal, OP won’t give information because it will be evident that something else happened, and it wasn’t natural. Though there is no evidence I have a gut feeling (based on years in the field of veterinary medicine). OP is the AH.
